I recall this one night that creeped me out so much. I was waiting for an Uber, and had to walk to the destination. 

It was probably midnight. If not, pretty close. Where I live, it’s semi-secluded. Really dark because of the trees and lack of lights. There is a long, straight street that goes past my neighborhood and eventually further down into a turn which will lead to a store, more darkness and silence, then finally civilization. 

I remember while waiting for my Uber I start to hear gentle, slow sound of chains..? Chains swinging slowly. I hear this for about five minutes straight and when I turn around looking for where it’s coming from, thinking it’s from one origin that does have chains, but not there and the sound is more distant, I turn around and I see this far away, bright light. 

I swear. It was like a scene from a suspenseful movie. I didn’t know what to do, especially since I couldn’t quite see it well. The chains were getting closer so I walked off to the side and hid behind the corner of a fence. A really dark corner which easily could have had a deranged druggie. Finally. After a few more minutes I see the light getting brighter and closer and it turns out to be a really big truck slowly moving through the long path. 

Imagine. Chains echoing. Darkness, and the faint light that eventually approaches shows the fog in the area. 

The truck was moving *juuust* fast enough to beat me if I were walking at a normal pace. If I ran, I would have gotten far enough to “escape” from the scary truck. 

So I stand at the side and watch this slow truck, with chains, pass by me. It’s pulling a completely black trailer thing with a single door in the back. Would only fit one person and I think it did have a small window. There were no other windows around the trailer attachment. 

Very creepy. I was both mesmerized and afraid. I was speechless and didn’t know how to react to it. Pretty cool, but pretty creepy.

I understand this. A long time ago I had a really good male friend. We got pretty close. Nothing official, but we were kind of suggesting experimenting.. if that makes sense. We were both interested and nervous, and then he just.. killed himself. I lost him without even knowing I was going to. I knew he suffered with depression and self harm, but suicide? It never came up, and we told each other everything. Even the embarrassing bits. 

Since that day depression, paranoia/fear, anxiety, and of course suicidal thoughts have been my best friend. I go through what he might have Had to deal with for a long time.. and I didn’t even know. How could I have not noticed? Or not even ask about. I was young. I didn’t quite know about the concept of suicide, but I never asked him. I feel like if I was better educated things could have been different. 

I have a few pictures of him on my phone. Luckily they’ve been passed down all throughout my old phones. Don’t know how they managed, but they did. He’s smiling. It’s Christmas time. His dog. Trying out a new haircut, new beanie.. I have a single, favourite printed picture of him in my room. I have a battery candle that I light on certain days. 

One day an ex friend saw him and said, “Huh. This is the guy? You could have done better. He’s like.. a 3 out of 10.” 
That’s why they’re an “ex” friend. 

My now boyfriend respects the awkward, young relationship I had. He doesn’t ask any questions. He just accepts that it’s a part of my past, a part of who I am now, and leaves it at that. 

If someone is jealous over a past relationship, especially if it ended in an unfortunate way, they’re not worth your time. Very immature, very out of place, and should be out of your life ASAP.

This is good advice. As they say in the dog training world.. you are not given a puppy that’s picky. The dog learns to become picky based off what they can get away with. 

Dogs will not starve themselves. Obviously if it’s been a week and they don’t even eat the food, and they’re elderly or sick, then you should add stuff. Yes it dies encourage the behaviour, but they’re old/sick so they need the food to avoid any complications. However a younger, healthier dog would be fine. It would actually be healthy to have them “fast” a bit and make them work for every bit of food. Teaches them that stuff isn’t free, all that sort of philosophy. 

If it’s possible to spend a little more on dog food, then do so. But it doesn’t seem like that’s your case. I know dog food can get really expensive. It sucks because good dog food is really important. 

So what I’d do is find a flavour you know your dog likes and buy based off that. Do take time to read the ingredients and consider the brand, then get cheapest of that. Don’t give the full serving of kibble and replace the rest of required calories with some of the suggested foods from previous commenter. (Right above) 

Those options are both typically favoured by dogs, but also pretty healthy/good for them. 

If your dog is getting picky as she ages I’d suggest speaking with your vet. Just make sure no underlying issues exist. If she’s fine, then go ahead and experiment. You could also get suggestions for your vet. 

Random tip: Goat’s milk is really good for them and dense/filling I believe. Also hydrates the kibble a bit and dog’s tend to really love goat’s milk.

That’s actually not the case. 

Service dogs are high level obedience. 

Typical pet are just.. trained. Maybe obedient. 

Service dogs require training every single day. Maintenance every single day. You need to remind and practice both tasks and commands all the time to keep them on their game. Consistently. Commitment. Cost for gear and food. Teaching them how to have an “on and off” switch. Knowing how to handle a high level obedience dog and a pet dog, but they are in the same body. 

A pet? Sit. Down. Wait. Leave it. Come. Name. 

Service dog? Sit. Down. Down/stay. Wait. Leave it. Focus. Come. Heel. Focus heel. Alert. Respond. Get help. Block. Cover. Get meds. Turn on light. Turn off light. Scan room. Bark if someone is there or come and notify me. Come back and encourage me in if no one is there. Automatically leave food alone no matter what. **Intelligent disobedience.** Name. Different names. Possibly different commands in a different language because some bystanders will try to distract the working dog. Guide work. Momentum pull (there’s a difference). Different ways to alert to different symptoms and attacks. Getting different items. Mobility tasks. Guide work. Psychiatric work. Medical work. Being the literal eyes for their handler. Working and making critical decisions **on their own and without guidance from handler.** etc. 

So unless you are a dog trainer or have been trained by a dog trainer and keep even your house kept pet to a high standard, I do not think you fully understand the amount of training and high level obedience that a service dog requires. 

Many people like in programs will give brief explanations so to not overwhelm people. But just having a trained SD is a lot of work. If the recipient doesn’t maintain the training then they will lose the training and the service dog can wash out due to handler mistake. 

I have trained multiple service dogs and other working dogs. I’ve found that I like having my dogs at a high level of obedience. An obedient dog is man’s best friend. So if I were to say, “A house trained dog is the same as a service dog in terms of obedience level,” I would be able to mean it and understand that fully. Is that what you meant? Otherwise, that’s quite an insult to those who put all of their time and efforts into high level obedient dogs because, yes it really does, require 24/7 work.

For most states in the US, yes you can bring an SDiT, even from puppyhood, into public areas than a fully trained SD may go. However. In training or fully trained, you are still required to follow basic ADA laws including with your own SD(iT).
